argument_markdown:
Source-backed input: RED-0001 is exactly the fixed list (3,12), (5,8), (6,6), (7,4), (8,0), (8,1), (8,2). No other source-backed assertion or dependency is used.

Proved steps. Let Gamma be the dual graph of the generic curve in an irreducible boundary divisor of Mbar_{5,8}. It has one edge. For each vertex v, let n_v count both original labeled legs and incident half-edges. Normalizing the unique node gives the clutching atlas attached to Gamma, and forgetting an ordering of graph data gives the stack quotient [Mbar_Gamma/Aut(Gamma)].

If the edge is a loop, normalization leaves the curve connected. Normalization lowers its genus from 5 to 4 and replaces the node by two marked branches. Thus the ordered atlas is Mbar_{4,10}. Exchanging the two branches does not change the glued curve and is the full graph automorphism group, so the normalized stack component is [Mbar_{4,10}/S_2]. Its sole atlas factor has type (4,10), outside RED-0001.

If the edge is separating, normalization has two connected components. Write their genera as g1,g2 and their inclusive marking counts as n1,n2. Additivity of arithmetic genus across a separating node gives g1+g2=5. Each of the eight original legs occurs once, and the normalized node supplies one half-edge on each component, so n1+n2=8+2=10. Each component is stable, hence 2g_i-2+n_i>0. The clutching atlas is Mbar_{g1,n1} x Mbar_{g2,n2}, modulo Aut(Gamma). Since g1+g2 is odd, the two vertex genera differ; consequently no graph automorphism exchanges the vertices, although retaining the quotient notation is the stack-theoretically correct convention.

For a genus-5 factor, the other vertex has genus 0. Stability of that rational vertex gives n_0 at least 3, hence n_5=10-n_0 at most 7. Therefore type (5,8) cannot occur. For a genus-3 factor, the other vertex has genus 2 and carries at least its incident half-edge, so n_2 is at least 1 and n_3=10-n_2 is at most 9. Therefore type (3,12) cannot occur. In every separating graph both genera are nonnegative and sum to 5, while the non-separating factor has genus 4. Thus no factor has genus 6, 7, or 8, excluding (6,6), (7,4), (8,0), (8,1), and (8,2). This exhausts the RED-0001 list.

Computational hypotheses: none. Gaps: none. Failed-route audit: the proof uses only one-edge stable-graph combinatorics and stability. It uses no virtual-cohomological-dimension vanishing, undecorated top-weight graph complex, point counting, or forgetful-map/local-system comparison. It makes no cohomological, Tate, determinant-edge, or H^{16}(Mbar_{5,8};Q) assertion.

claims.statement: The stacky non-separating normalization is [Mbar_{4,10}/S_2], with S_2 exchanging the two branches of the node.
Every separating one-edge normalization has ordered atlas Mbar_{g1,n1} x Mbar_{g2,n2}, modulo Aut(Gamma), with g1+g2=5, n1+n2=10, and both vertices stable.
A genus-5 separating factor has at most 7 inclusive markings, and a genus-3 separating factor has at most 9 inclusive markings.
No factor in any irreducible one-edge boundary normalization of Mbar_{5,8} has a type in the RED-0001 residual list.

summary: Classifying one-edge dual graphs of stable 8-pointed genus-5 curves gives the stacky non-separating normalization [Mbar_{4,10}/S_2] and separating product atlases whose inclusive marking counts sum to 10. Stability and edge incidence give the required genus-5 and genus-3 bounds, excluding every RED-0001 pair.
theorem_statement: Every factor occurring in the normalization of an irreducible boundary divisor of Mbar_{5,8} lies outside the RED-0001 residual list. The non-separating component is [Mbar_{4,10}/S_2]. A separating one-edge graph has ordered atlas Mbar_{g1,n1} x Mbar_{g2,n2} with g1+g2=5, n1+n2=10, and both vertices stable, modulo Aut(Gamma). In particular a genus-5 factor has at most 7 markings and a genus-3 factor has at most 9 markings, so no factor is one of (3,12), (5,8), (6,6), (7,4), (8,0), (8,1), or (8,2). This theorem makes no Tate assertion and does not conclude H^{16}(Mbar_{5,8};Q).
